c: What the dbt Analytics Engineering Certification Exam looks like: format, scoring, rules and question types.
The 7 official topics and their 31 sub-objectives, and where each one is taught in this bible.
A 14-week study plan, a daily routine and a progress tracker you will fill in yourself.

Many people fail certification exams not because the topics are too hard, but because they study the wrong things, in the wrong order, without practice. This chapter gives you the map before the journey: what the exam really tests, how the questions look, and a plan that takes you from zero to ready. Read it once now, and come back to it every week to check your progress.

This bible follows the official exam outline for dbt Core 1.11, one objective at a time, starting from the basics (data, command line, Git, SQL, YAML, Jinja). Every chapter mixes explanation, hands-on labs and exam-style questions, because the exam rewards people who have
dbt, not people who memorised it. If you finish every lab, the capstone project and the three mock exams, you will be ready to pass with a strong score.
This book has one purpose: to take you from zero to the

c: Memory fades fast unless you revisit things at growing intervals. After you finish a chapter, review it (summary box + your error notebook entries + redo the wrong questions):
Finish the chapter and its quiz.
Re-read the summary box; redo the questions you missed.
Explain the three-sentence idea out loud, without notes.
Redo the full quiz. Aim for 90% or more.

After each chapter, try to explain the main idea in simple words, in French or in English, as if to a friend who does not work with data. If you get stuck, you found exactly what to review. This is called the Feynman technique.

The exam: 65 questions, 2 hours, 65% to pass, $200, online and proctored, not open book, dbt Core 1.11.
One point per question, no negative marking, some unscored questions: always answer everything.
Six formats: multiple choice, fill in the blank, matching, hotspot, build list and DOMC (one option at a time, no going back).
